with the anchor moved to the session's own version the same files parse `ok: true` in full. The
Phase 4 blackout was this same defect one window further out. A tolerance measured in patch releases
is a countdown, not a policy.

**`src/parser/fingerprint.ts` is the authority.** `PINNED_CC_VERSION` is the anchor, `VERSION_WINDOW`
is the allowance, `isVersionAccepted` is the predicate, and `versionWindow()` materialises the
corners. The numbers live in that module and nowhere else; this section names them once so a reader
has them, and a release test asserts these words against those constants.

- **The version string is no longer the compatibility test.** It refuses two things and nothing
  else: a **major** component differing from the anchor's, and a **minor** component more than **1**
  away from the anchor's. The **patch component is not compared at all** — `2.1.999` is read exactly
  as `2.1.246` is. A version that is not strictly `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (`2.1`, `2.1.246-beta`,
  `02.1.246`) still refuses, because guessing at an unrecognised string is the failure this module
  exists to prevent.
- **Anchor: `2.1.246`. Window: major exact, minor +/-1** — `2.0.x` through `2.2.x`.
- **`PINNED_CC_VERSION` is a provenance anchor, not a support claim.** It names the version whose
  committed fixture proved the structure the fingerprint asserts: `fixtures/cc-2.1.246/`, harvested
  from this repo's own session on 2026-08-26. It moves when, and only when, a new fixture is
  harvested and the structure is re-proved against it. It is not moved to chase a release, and
  moving it is not how a compatibility problem gets fixed.
- **The structural fingerprint is the whole in-range story.** Within the window the only thing that
  can refuse a session is structure: the required keys per entry `type` (`REQUIRED_ENTRY_FIELDS`),
  the required sidecar join keys (`REQUIRED_META_FIELDS`), and the subagent directory layout. Those
  refusal codes are unchanged. **Unknown fields are kept and never refused** — Claude Code adds
  fields between releases, and `2.1.241` added `atis` while the slices we hold carry no `requestId`,
  both without consequence. A line whose `type` is unrecognised is **counted and skipped** by the
  line parser (`parse.ts`, rejection `unknownType`), degrading one line rather than the session.
- **Out-of-window, malformed and unparseable versions refuse exactly as before**: `unsupportedVersion`,
  the session renders `unsupported`, never a partial tree (G3). A file whose version changes partway
  through is accepted while every version in it stays in range, and refused as `versionChangedMidFile`
  once the drift leaves it. Both codes and both stories are unchanged.

**What this buys and what it costs.** It buys the thing the product exists for: it keeps working
across the patch releases Claude Code actually ships, which arrive faster than any capture cadence
can follow. It costs the guarantee that every accepted byte came from a captured release — an
accepted version nobody captured is a version nobody verified, so structural drift inside the range
surfaces as a **wrong tree** rather than an honest refusal. That is precisely why the structural
assertions are the tripwire and why they were not softened alongside the string: the two moved in
opposite directions deliberately. The upgrade story is unchanged — when the structure moves, harvest
fixtures from this repo's own sessions first, re-anchor, then change code (G6).

**Corpus at this amendment.** `fixtures/cc-2.1.234/` (the layout and join capture, with a
`spawnDepth: 2` agent and an offloaded `tool-results/` payload) · `fixtures/cc-2.1.237/`
(content-destroyed drift witness) · `fixtures/cc-2.1.241/` (a session on a local `local-model` model:
flat, no subagents, carrying `atis` / `atis-latch` and an unrecognised file inside the session
directory) · `fixtures/cc-2.1.246/` (the anchor — an R1 mirror pair carrying one subagent and its
sidecar) · `fixtures/synthetic-structure-2.1.246/` (hand-mutated: an in-range version with a
required key renamed, which must still refuse).

I've completed Phase 0 (load, read, re-measure). Before dispatching anything, here's what measurement says — including two places where the documents are stale.

## Re-measurement vs. the documents

| Claim | Source | Measured now | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tree clean, `release/0.5.0` | HANDOVER §8 | clean, 17 commits ahead of `origin` | ✅ agrees |
| Privacy sweep passes | HANDOVER §1 | `unexpected=0 secrets=0 foreign=0`, 23 advisories, exit 0 | ✅ agrees |
| "All 30 sessions map to project `499645fc…`; `global` has zero" | HANDOVER §7 | **31 sessions, 3 project rows** — agent-deck 29, **`ERW` 1**, **`global` 1** | ❌ **stale** |
| "Phase 3 needs a live OpenCode session from the user" | HANDOVER §7 | **Not needed** — the `1.18.22` subset already satisfies every DoD 3.3 item | ❌ **stale, in our favour** |
| DB holds `1.18.21` × 5, `1.18.22` × 23 | HANDOVER §4 | `1.18.21` × 5, `1.18.22` × **26** (24 of them agent-deck's) | ⚠️ moved |

**DoD 3.3 coverage inside the `1.18.22` agent-deck subset** (24 sessions, 865 parts, 3,179 events) — all present, nothing to manufacture:

completed tools 219 · error tools 27 · reasoning parts 167 (max 36,716 chars) · agreeing task pairs 20 · **`task` parts with no `sessionId` 9** · step-finish with non-zero tokens 147 · event-cursor rows 24 · compaction 1 · inline outputs ≥50k **23** (max 88,292) · concurrent sessions **0** (the DoD's "if present" branch).

**Content safety, checked case-sensitively:** 0 `ERW`, 0 `ghp_`/`github_pat_`/`sk-ant-`/`AKIA`/`xox?-` hits; the only `projects/<project>` path in the whole subset is `agent-deck` (55). *(An earlier pass showed alarming counts — SQLite's `LIKE` is case-insensitive, so `ACCESS_TOKEN` was matching `access_token` in this repo's own contract doc and `ERW` was matching `ov**erw**rite`. `GLOB` is the case-sensitive operator; the clean numbers are the real ones.)*

Four decisions I can't take for you:

questions.question: DoD 3.2 says the capture "aborts on any `project` row whose `worktree` is not this repo (G8)". Taken literally that now makes the capture impossible — the live DB has an `ERW` project row (1 session) and a `global` row (1 session, cwd `<HOME>`). How should G8 be enforced?

options.label: Filter, don't abort (Recommended)
options.description: Select only the agent-deck project row and its sessions/messages/parts/events; abort only if a row SELECTED FOR CAPTURE resolves to a foreign worktree. Foreign rows never enter the fixture, and the script logs exactly what it excluded into the README. G8's intent (only agent-deck is observed) holds; the DoD wording gets amended in 3.1 to say so.

options.label: Literal abort
options.description: Keep the wording. The capture stays blocked until the ERW and global sessions leave the live DB — which is a write to OpenCode's data directory, so G1 forbids Agent Deck doing it and it would be you, by hand, destructively.

options.label: Fresh scratch DB
options.description: Drive OpenCode against a scratch XDG_DATA_HOME (measured working in 2.6) to build a DB that is clean by construction. But the entire harvest set then has to be re-manufactured: 27 error tool parts, 9 sessionId-less task parts, an 88 KB inline output, the compaction row. Days, not hours.

questions.question: The `1.18.22` agent-deck subset is ~17 MB of JSON (part 5.90 MB, event 10.90 MB, message 0.31 MB); the live DB file is 24.7 MB and this repo's entire `.git` is currently 7.3 MB. DoD 3.2 allows truncating "other long payloads to shape with the decision recorded". How aggressive?

options.label: Stub event.data only (Recommended)
options.description: Contract §6: the engine reads seq and type only from `event`, taking content from the content tables. So replace `event.data` with a shape-only stub — costs the engine nothing, keeps all 3,179 rows with real aggregate_id/seq/type so the cursor tap is genuine, saves ~10.9 MB. All part.data and message.data stay verbatim. Fixture lands ~7 MB.

options.label: Stub events + truncate tool output
options.description: As above, plus truncate tool `state.output` above a threshold, keeping the ≥50,000-char specimen (and one per status) verbatim. Tool outputs are 2.90 MB of the 5.90 MB. Fixture lands ~3-4 MB — but the parser's large-payload path is then pinned to fewer real specimens.

options.label: Verbatim, no truncation
options.description: Capture everything as-is. Strongest fixture-is-law posture, zero judgment calls to record — but a ~20 MB binary blob in a public repo that CI clones at fetch-depth 0, roughly tripling the repo.

questions.question: The two known `compaction` shapes are split across versions: `1.18.22` (the anchor) has the single row carrying `tail_start_id`; the two rows WITHOUT it are both in `1.18.21`. DoD 3.3 asks for "the compaction rows", plural.

options.label: 1.18.22 only, record the gap (Recommended)
options.description: PLAN-compliant: 3.3 already says take the newer set and record the older's presence. The README ticks compaction as captured-with-one-shape and states plainly that the no-`tail_start_id` variant exists in 1.18.21 and is NOT captured — so Phase 4 must treat `tail_start_id` as optional on the strength of a recorded observation, not a fixture.

options.label: Capture both versions as two corpora
options.description: `fixtures/opencode-1.18.22/` as the anchor plus `fixtures/opencode-1.18.21/` as a drift witness — exactly the pattern the CC corpus already uses (cc-2.1.246 anchor, cc-2.1.237/241 witnesses). Closes the shape gap with a real fixture and costs ~+2 MB and a second capture run. A deviation from 3.3's wording, so it gets recorded.

options.label: One DB, both version sets
options.description: Keep all 29 agent-deck sessions in a single fixture. Breaks the `opencode-<version>/` naming rule (version = the data's session.version) and muddies which version the anchor actually is.

questions.question: DoD 3.4 wants the expected `SessionState` tree committed as `golden.json`, generated "through a documented manual procedure this once". The harvest is 24 sessions / 865 parts — too large for anyone to derive or check by hand.

options.label: Full tree + hand-verified core (Recommended)
options.description: One standalone generator written from `docs/opencode-contract.md` (NOT from `src/opencode/`, which doesn't exist) emits golden.json over all 24 sessions as Phase 4's reproduction target — and the README documents a small named core (the task pair, the sessionId-less task part, the error tool, the compaction row, the 88 KB output) derived by hand and shown step by step. Honest about which half is actually eyeballed.

options.label: Named subset only
options.description: Golden covers only the hand-checkable named sessions. Every committed number is verified by a human — but Phase 4 then only has to reproduce the subset, and the other 20 sessions are pinned by nothing.

options.label: Full tree only
options.description: Machine-generated golden over all 24 sessions, no hand-verified core. Comprehensive regression target, but nobody can eyeball 865 parts, so it pins whatever the generator did rather than what the contract says.

## What the section must contain

Cover every item the DoD lists. Specifics you must get right, each traceable to a contract section:

- **Data location and format** — `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db`, SQLite in WAL
  mode, read with `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` `{ readOnly: true }` (contract §2, §7, amendment §A,
  §B). Note the config directory `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\` is under G1 too (amendment §B).
  Note the engine defines its **own** test override rather than relying on OpenCode's
  `XDG_DATA_HOME` resolution, and that the negative control fakes **`USERPROFILE`**, not `HOME`
  (contract §2, amendment §C).
- **Schema fingerprint target** — the six required tables and the columns the engine reads
  (contract §3). State the rule that every other table is **ignored, not refused** — the CC
  unknown-field rule applied to schema — and that the four/five secret-bearing tables are dropped
  from any fixture **by schema, not by row count**.
- **The join** — `task` part `state.metadata.sessionId` → child `session.id`, cross-assertable
  against child `session.parent_id` and the part's `state.metadata.parentSessionId`; a primary key
  in both directions (contract §5). **The parked case is load-bearing and must be in the spec:**
  of 30 `task` parts, **9 carry no `state.metadata.sessionId`** (amendment §G). That absence is a
  NORMAL STATE — most likely the call observed before the child row exists — and is the direct
  analogue of the recorded CC finding that a subagent sidecar appears 0.080–0.120 s before its
  transcript. The grafter **parks** it with a stable code (G3); it must not guess from timing and
  must not treat absence as a disagreement.
- **Liveness by event cursor, no socket** — contract §6. Per-session last-seen `seq`, `event_sequence`
  holds the max per aggregate, 120 s threshold reused from CC. Event type form is `name.N` (assert
  the FORM, do not pin the set). The re-read rule when an observed `seq` goes backwards: full
  re-read plus a counter, never a refusal. Events are read for **seq and type only**; content comes
  from the content tables, as separate queries — that separation is G2 *inside* the engine.
  **Also record (amendment §D) that a plugin/hook API DOES exist** and that the earlier
  "no hook mechanism" claim was an untested absence claim that turned out false — but that v0.5.0
  scope is unchanged: **zero sockets**, the cursor poll ships as designed, and a plugin tap could
  only ever be a user-pasted install because the config directory is under G1.
- **Version window** — anchored on the **data's** per-session `session.version`, never the binary's.
  State why in one line, with the measurement: the DB held `1.18.21` and `1.18.22` sessions while
  the binary went `1.18.22` → `1.18.23` mid-phase (amendment §H). Three versions at once. The
  concrete window belongs to Phase 4 and the capture — say that the anchor is the captured corpus
  and that the structural fingerprint is the compatibility story, exactly as G9 says for CC.
  **Do not invent a numeric window.**
- **Redaction (G4)** — reasoning parts dropped at the parse boundary. State the inversion of the CC
  trap explicitly: in CC the thinking text is empty and the bytes sit in `signature`; in OpenCode
  the bytes are plainly present in `part.data.text` (contract §4), so the G4 test here is real
  rather than vacuous and asserts against literal captured bytes. Any provider `signature`/metadata
  is dropped too.
- **Engine tag in `SessionState`** — sessions carry which engine observed them. Read
  `src/model/events.ts` for the actual `SessionState` shape and describe the tag in terms that
  match it. **You do not implement it** — you specify it. Name the two values.
- **Discovery** — `project.worktree` is an absolute path, so there is **no slug decoding**; it is
  matched case-insensitively against the workspace folders (contract §9). The Windows drive-letter
  case trap applies here exactly as it does to CC slugs.
- **A CC → OpenCode concept map** is already in contract §9. Reference it rather than duplicating it.

**Reference the contract doc by section throughout** (e.g. "contract §5", "contract amendment §G").
That is an explicit DoD requirement.

## Rules that bind you

- **G1 read-only:** your section must state that the engine writes nothing under either the OpenCode
  data or config directory, and that this is now enforced by SQLite itself — a write through the
  read-only handle throws `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR` errcode 8 (amendment §A). That refusal is the G1 proof.
- **Claim only what was measured.** Where the contract says something is unverified or was not
  reproduced, your spec says so too. The specific one that matters: §7's edge — OpenCode *dying* and
  leaving a hot WAL, where recovery needs write access — was **not** reproduced. The ordinary hot-WAL
  case is measured as a non-event (20/20 opens, 0 `SQLITE_BUSY`, 2 ms worst). Keep those apart.
- **Never write a raw control character into source.** Escapes, always.
- **Backticks inside a shell-quoted string are command substitution.** This repo has lost content to
  this four times, including in `git commit -m`. Write your commit message to a file with a real
  editor tool and use `git commit -F <file>`. Do not write file content through
  `node -e "..."` or a quoted heredoc — use your Write/Edit tools.

## Budget law (standing user direction — it is enforced)

Write the whole section first, then check it ONCE. **You are editing one Markdown file: do not run
the test suite at all, and never run the full suite.** Verification for this package is
`npm run lint` only if you somehow touched a lintable file (you should not have).

## Report format

Report DONE with:
1. **Files changed** — full list with line counts (`git diff --stat` against your merge-base).
2. **DoD 3.1 coverage** — one line per DoD item (data location · fingerprint target · join +
   parked case · liveness cursor · version window · redaction · engine tag · discovery · references
   contract by section), each with the heading in your section that covers it.
3. **Evidence** — the exact section title line, the output of
   `git log --oneline -1` on your branch, and `git diff --stat`.
4. **Deviations** — anything you could not do, anything you believe needs a file you do not own,
   and any place the contract doc and the spec disagree.

**Part types (anchor):** tool 246 · step-start 176 · reasoning 167 · step-finish 147 · text 113 ·

**Tool names (anchor):** bash 95 · read 73 · task 29 · grep 17 · edit 17 · webfetch 7 · glob 4 ·

**Do not file-copy the live DB, and do not `VACUUM INTO`.** Build each fixture DB from scratch:

1. Open the live DB read-only (`{ readOnly: true }`). It is never written, opened writable, or
   touched in any other way. This is G1 and it is the whole point.
2. Read the source DDL out of `sqlite_master` for the tables you keep, and create the fixture DB
   with **that exact DDL**, so the fixture's schema is the real schema and the Phase 4 fingerprint
   is pinned to real bytes.
3. **Drop by schema — never create these tables at all:** `account`, `account_state`,
   `control_account`, `credential`, `session_share`. Note the DoD names four; the fifth
   (`account_state`) comes from the Phase 2 handoff. **Drop all five** — a superset is the safe
   direction. Record the superset decision in the README.
4. **Keep** the non-secret out-of-scope tables (`data_migration`, `migration`, `permission`,
   `project_directory`, `session_context_epoch`, `session_input`, `session_message`, `todo`,
   `workspace`) — empty or filtered as appropriate. They exist so Phase 4 has a real fixture for
   the "unknown tables are ignored, not refused" rule (contract §3). Say so in the README.
5. Insert the filtered rows verbatim. **Preserve exactly, unmodified:** every `id`, `callID`,
   `parent_id`, `project_id`, `session_id`, `message_id`, `aggregate_id`, `seq`,
   `state.metadata.sessionId`, `state.metadata.parentSessionId`, every `time_*` value, and every
   reasoning `text` byte. These are the join keys and the G4 target; a normalised fixture pins
   nothing.
6. Keep the `project` row for agent-deck. Do not rewrite its `worktree` — this developer's own
   absolute paths are deliberate inside an enumerated fixture corpus (that is repo law: the privacy
   sweep's `-> 0` applies to FOREIGN content and secrets, not to this developer's own paths).

   target `session.version` as parameters rather than hard-coding one corpus.

- **SQLite `LIKE` is CASE-INSENSITIVE.** `data LIKE '%ERW%'` matches `ov`+`erw`+`rite` and
  `ACCESS_TOKEN` matches this repo's own prose. The orchestrator burned a probe on exactly this.
  **Any needle or G8 check you write must use `GLOB`** (case-sensitive) or an explicit
  `instr(data, 'X') > 0`. If you report a needle count from `LIKE`, your number is wrong.

  2 h 30 m while the DB grew 425 KB. SQLite reuses WAL frames in place. Never build a check on it.
- **Never ask the binary its version.** OpenCode self-updated `1.18.22` → `1.18.23` mid-session
  during Phase 2. The version of a corpus is its **data's** `session.version`, always. If you invoke
  OpenCode at all (you should not need to), the real binary is under
  `%APPDATA%/npm/node_modules/opencode-ai/node_modules/opencode-windows-x64/bin/` — the thing on
  `PATH` is a broken npm shim.

  this four times, including inside `git commit -m`. **Write your commit message to a file and use
  `git commit -F <file>`.** Never write file content through `node -e "..."` or a quoted heredoc —
  use your Write/Edit tools. A quoted heredoc through the Bash tool is not reliably literal either
  (measured: `\\b` arrived as one backslash and `\\s` as two, on the same line).
- **No shebang in a `.mjs` file.** vite's hashbang strip is `/^#!.*\n/` and `.` does not match `\r`,
  so a shebang breaks vitest COLLECTION in a CRLF checkout only — green for you, `SyntaxError` for
  everyone else. `scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs` has no shebang for exactly this reason. Match it.
- **Never write a raw control character into source.** Escapes, always.
- **Source files in this tree are CRLF; `fixtures/` is LF and marked `-text`.** Your `.db` files are
  binary and `.gitattributes` already covers them via `fixtures/** -text` — but only because they go
  under `fixtures/`. Do not put them anywhere else.

  next harvest and read as regressions. Derive from the corpus, or assert behaviour. (The README
  is the right place for the numbers; a test is not.)

DoD 3.2's last sentence: *"Replay from a clean checkout with `USERPROFILE` faked fails loudly
(test)."* Requirements:

- **Fake `USERPROFILE`, not `HOME`.** `os.homedir()` reads `USERPROFILE` on Windows. Faking only
  `HOME` runs happily against the REAL data directory and reports a confident green pass on the one
  check whose entire purpose is proving we never touch it. This is measured, recorded repo history,
  and it is the single most important line in this package.

  missing root. It must NOT silently fall back to the live DB, and it must NOT pass by accident.

  source is opened with `readOnly: true` and that a write through that handle throws
  `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR` (errcode 8) — that refusal is the measured G1 proof.

  required ones (`project`, `session`, `message`, `part`, `event`, `event_sequence`).
- Assert G8 over the committed corpora: every `project.worktree` in each fixture resolves to this
  repo, case-insensitively. Remember the Windows drive-letter case trap (`c--Users-…` and
  `C--Users-…` both occur) — match case-insensitively.

  needs an environment gate, note that the repo's rule is that **every skip is accounted for by
  GATE, not against a number**; a suite that fails to COLLECT reports as "skipped" and reads green.

## The README each corpus needs (DoD 3.2 + 3.3)

Version · capture time · the exact procedure (reproducible command) · the session ids taken ·
**the DoD 3.3 checklist with every item ticked and the evidence beside it** · what was excluded and
why (the two foreign sessions, by id and worktree) · the five dropped tables and that they were
dropped by schema at 0 rows · the no-truncation decision and the resulting byte sizes · the
compaction-shape split and which corpus witnesses which · concurrent sessions absent, with the query
and its empty result · max spawn depth 1 and the contract §5 reason. Look at
`fixtures/cc-2.1.246/README.md` for the house style before writing yours.

**Write all the code first, then run.** When you are done writing, run **only your own test file**
(`node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/release/opencode-capture.test.ts`), fix what it
reports, run it once more. That is the budget. **NEVER run the full test suite** — the orchestrator
does that once, at the end. `npx vitest` can die mid-run at exit 127 or -1073740791 with no failing
assertion; `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` is the reliable invocation.

Also run `npm run typecheck` once at the end (**two** tsc projects; zero errors expected) and
`npm run lint` once. `vitest` and `tsc` disagree about duplicate imports and **vitest is the one
that lies** — a green test file is not a typecheck.

**Wave 1 closed, wave 2 dispatched.** P3-GOLDEN and P3-SWEEP are running.

**P3-CAPTURE merged** (`b7e1a5d`-ish, on the phase branch). Both corpora are in:

| | anchor `1.18.22` | witness `1.18.21` |
|---|---|---|
| sessions | 24 | 5 |
| completed / error tool parts | 219 / 27 | 98 / 1 |
| `task` parts with **no** `sessionId` | **9 of 29** | 0 of 1 |
| agreeing join pairs | 20 | 1 |
| compaction | 1 row **with** `tail_start_id` | 2 rows **without** |
| longest inline tool output | 88,292 chars | 53,308 |

Row counts match the pre-capture recon exactly. The capture doesn't file-copy or `VACUUM INTO` — it reads the DDL out of `sqlite_master` and rebuilds from it, so the live DB is never opened writable. Verbatim preservation is verified two ways per table: a SHA-256 over every column of every row, and a second hash over SQLite's own `length(CAST(data AS BLOB))` so the check lands on stored bytes rather than decoded strings.

**Three implementer deviations I accepted**, all recorded in the merge commit:

The one worth your attention: **foreign worktrees are redacted in the committed READMEs** (root plus a segment count), full paths going to the console only. The worker's reasoning is that a README naming another project's absolute path in a public repo is precisely the foreign content the G8 filter exists to exclude — a G8 log that is itself a G8 violation. I think that's right. Project ids and session counts stay verbatim, so the exclusion is still auditable. It's one function and one README section if you want it reversed.

Also: the script **refuses to run** if the source DB has a table in neither the keep-plan nor the drop-list, so the next OpenCode schema change fails the capture deliberately rather than silently absorbing a new table. That's G3 applied to the capture itself, and I'd rather have it.

**On the size, now measured rather than estimated:** 25,137,152 bytes on disk pack to roughly **5.6 MB** — the witness deltifies against the anchor down to 609 KB, since they share a schema and overlapping content. The **entire repository pack is 9.27 MiB**, which is the whole clone cost. My earlier warning about "roughly tripling the repo" was pessimistic; the verbatim decision is cheap and I'd not revisit it.

Two things I'm carrying forward rather than letting them evaporate: **`SessionState.projectSlug` has no OpenCode answer** (Phase 5 owns it, and PLAN's DoD 5.1/5.2 don't currently decide it), and the sweep now has 25 MB of binary to scan — P3-SWEEP is under instruction to measure the runtime against the 168 ms / 462 ms baseline and report rather than quietly excluding the fixtures.

Still unanswered from my side: **what "the live addon" actually is.** That determines whether the F1 subagent-sidecar theory is worth anything.

**P3-SWEEP merged** (`56e115d`). Three of four packages are in; P3-GOLDEN is still running.

**DoD 3.5 is satisfied:** sweep exit 0 with `unexpected=0 secrets=0 foreign=0`, `--untracked` exit 0, `privacy.test.ts` 52 passed / 0 skipped.

The worker did the thing I'd hoped for on `CAPTURE_CORPORA`: **verified rather than assumed**. `fixtures/` was already a top-level prefix, so both corpora were inside the FOREIGN gate before it touched anything — and it ran *both* directions of the completeness guard (every tracked top-level dir covered; no enumerated prefix matching nothing) rather than just the one that would have looked green.

**The performance cost, measured:**

| leg | before | after | bytes scanned |
|---|---|---|---|
| working tree | 161 ms | **883 ms** (5.5×) | 6.7 MB → 32.0 MB |
| history | 435 ms | **981 ms** (2.3×) | 19.0 MB → 44.6 MB |

Both stay an order of magnitude under the 10,000 ms bound the suite holds the history leg to. The diagnosis is the interesting part and worth keeping: **the dominant term is per-hit, not per-byte** — ~356 ms of the ~720 ms delta is path-token classification over 22,394 identifier hits, against ~113 ms of read + decode + index. So the sweep's cost scales with how often your own path appears *inside* a corpus, not with corpus size. Anyone who later concludes "the big fixture made the sweep slow" will be wrong.

Two results that keep the zeros from being vacuous, which is the failure mode this repo has been bitten by: `foreign=0` came after the foreign regexes matched **1,320 candidate values** across the two corpora, every one naming `agent-deck` — the gate fired and returned zero rather than never firing. And NUL bytes didn't truncate the scan: 22,394 hits were extracted from inside the two binaries, which a grep-based reader couldn't have produced.

**One correction I'm queuing rather than making now.** The third ALLOW rule (`capture-script-needles`, for the capture script's 12 hits) is the right call — it matches the `sweep-needles` precedent one file over, is scoped to a single file, and ALLOW only affects the identifier leg, so SECRET and FOREIGN still gate that file. But its reason string is wrong twice: the needle is **`projects`**, not the cloud-sync folder it names, and the claim that *"a GLOB pattern handed to SQLite has to be the literal string"* is false — the pattern sits in a template literal and could take a fragmented constant, as could the regex. Keeping the rule is correct; recording a constraint that doesn't exist is not. I'm holding the fix until P3-GOLDEN merges, because editing `privacy-sweep.mjs` now would invalidate the report's recorded head and break the freshness guard.

Also queued for the same commit: `fixtures/README.md` still calls `origin` **private**. It's public. That's a false claim about itself in a public repo, and the worker correctly left it as out-of-scope rather than quietly widening its remit.

`report.json` grew 118 KB → 1.1 MB on the new advisories. The worker declined to add truncation, which I agree with — no rule truncates today and inventing one here would change what the report means everywhere else. Recorded as a repo-weight question for a later phase.

P3 glue: correct two documentation claims that were false

Orchestrator edits, recorded as deviations because the phase protocol says the
orchestrator writes glue only. Neither changes behaviour; both correct a statement
that a reader would have believed.

1. scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs — the capture-script-needles reason string.

   It described the needle as the cloud-sync folder holding this developer's
   projects. Measured: the needle is the project-holding directory one level
   below that, 12 occurrences, and it appears as a comment, a regex literal,
   three SQL GLOB patterns and one line of generated README.

   It also claimed the term could not be assembled from fragments "because a
   GLOB pattern handed to SQLite has to be the literal string". That is false: a
   GLOB pattern is a runtime value and can be built from fragments exactly the
   way sweep-needles builds its own needles. The rule itself is kept — it matches
   the sweep-needles precedent one file over, it is scoped to a single file, and
   ALLOW governs only the identifier leg so SECRET and FOREIGN still gate that
   file. What is corrected is the justification, which now says the term could be
   fragmented and records why it was left whole.

   A reason string in this file is load-bearing documentation rather than
   decoration, and one asserting a constraint that does not exist would be
   repeated by whoever reads it next.

2. fixtures/README.md — the "Privacy: status after the Phase 1 scrub" section
   stated that origin was private and listed two gates on "any public flip". The
   flip happened after Phase 5. A tracked file in a public repository asserting
   that the repository is private is exactly the stale-state class CLAUDE.md
   names as this repo's most repeated defect. The section is kept as the record
   of what was required before the flip, with the false sentence replaced by the
   current fact and a pointer to docs/evidence/privacy/README.md as the
   authority.

Not fixed here and left for the handoff: src/release/workflow.test.ts carries the
same stale claim in a file-header comment. It is a comment rather than an
assertion, this phase does not otherwise touch that file, and superseding stale
state documents is the handoff's job.

docs/evidence/privacy/report.json is regenerated in the NEXT commit, not this one.
The head-freshness guard asserts git log <report.head>..HEAD -- scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs
is empty, so the report must be regenerated with this change already in history.

Run the FULL test suite for the `agent-deck` repository at
`<HOME>/projects/agent-deck`, currently on branch
`phase-3-oc-spec-harvest`. This is the v0.5.0 Phase 3 gate run.

## The invocation

Use **`node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run`** from the repo root.

Do NOT use `npm test` or `npx vitest`. Both are unreliable here and it is measured, not folklore:
the `npm` shim intermittently exits 127, and `npx vitest` has died mid-run twice with **no failing
assertion and no summary line** — exit 127 at ~19 of 40 files, and exit -1073740791 (0xC0000409) at
~6 of 40 files. Neither code is stable and neither is a fingerprint of a cause. The `node
node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` form is the fix and produces identical totals.

## Also run, each once

- `npm run typecheck` — **TWO** tsc projects (host, no DOM lib; plus webview). Zero errors expected.
  A green test file is not a typecheck: `vitest` and `tsc` disagree about duplicate imports and
  vitest is the one that lies.
- `npm run lint` — eslint flat config, zero errors expected.

## Report exactly

1. **Exact counts**: test files passed/failed, tests passed/failed/skipped, duration, exit code.
2. **Every failure in full** — file, test name, the assertion message, and enough of the diff to act
   on. Do not summarise a failure.
3. **The skip count, accounted for BY GATE, not against a number.** This is a real requirement, not
   boilerplate. A suite that fails to COLLECT reports as "skipped" and reads green in the summary
   line — that has happened in this repo and zero assertions ran while the totals looked healthy.
   There are four environment-conditional gates:
   - `runIf(AGENT_DECK_PACKAGE_AUDIT === '1')` in `src/release/vsix.test.ts`
   - `skipIf(!WSL.usable)` twice, in `src/model/pathmatrix.test.ts` (one describe of 6, plus one test)
   - `skipIf(LIVE_SETTINGS === null)` in `src/release/readme.test.ts`
   Name which gate accounts for each skip you observe. **Any skip you cannot attribute to one of
   those four is a defect — say so explicitly.** On this dev box three of the four gates are live,
   so the healthy count is normally 1.
4. **Timing note**: `src/perf/perf.test.ts` is ~31-42 s and IS the suite's critical path. Report its
   duration separately so a slow run can be attributed.
5. Whether `src/release/vsix.test.ts` needed to build anything mid-run (it builds missing bundles in
   its `beforeAll`; `vsce ls` reports files that EXIST, so that file's assertions depend on build
   state and it memoises the listing at module scope).

## Context you need

This phase added roughly 25 MB of binary SQLite fixture under `fixtures/opencode-1.18.22/` and
`fixtures/opencode-1.18.21/`, plus four new/changed test surfaces:
`src/release/opencode-capture.test.ts` (53 tests), `src/release/opencode-golden.test.ts` (78 tests),
and changes to `scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs` affecting `src/release/privacy.test.ts` (52 tests).

**`src/release/privacy.test.ts` is now materially slower** — the sweep it exercises went from
~161 ms / ~435 ms per leg to ~740 ms / ~1032 ms because of the new binary corpora. That is expected
and both legs remain far under the 10,000 ms bound the file asserts. Report its duration.

**One diagnosis rule that matters more than any fix:** a suite failure that disappears on a second
run is a defect report about the test, not noise to re-roll. This repo lost four phases to
re-running a suite to "see if it was flaky". If something fails, report it — do not re-run to check
whether it passes the second time.

**Do not fix anything.** Report only. I route failures back to the package that owns the file.

## Budget

ONE full-suite run, plus the typecheck and the lint. If the suite dies mid-run with no summary line
(the measured failure mode above), that is a result worth reporting — say where it died and at what
exit code, then run it once more, and report both. Nothing else.

**The gate run found one real defect — and it's a good catch, not a nuisance.**

`src/hooks/egress.test.ts` failed. Not an assertion: the `beforeAll` at line 242 timed out at vitest's **10 s default** while running a synchronous esbuild subprocess retried up to 3×. The fix was already sitting in the same file — the sibling hook at line 600 closes with `}, 120_000)`. The author budgeted the heavier hook and left this one on the default. It fit until Phase 3 made the suite heavier (`privacy.test.ts` ~1 s → 9.2 s on the new corpora, plus ~2 s of new files), which pushed this file into a window alongside `vsix.test.ts` and `webview/capture.test.ts`.

**Why it mattered more than a timeout usually does.** The summary line read:

```
Test Files  1 failed | 42 passed (43)
Tests       1570 passed | 7 skipped (1577)
```

No failed-*test* count at all — a suite-level failure contributes none. The timeout marked the whole describe as **six skips**, and six G5 zero-egress assertions over the shipped bundle ran **zero times** while the tests line looked clean. That's the recorded "fails to COLLECT, reports as skipped, reads green" class arriving by a new route. What surfaced it was insisting the runner account for every skip **by gate** rather than against a number: four environment gates exist, the healthy count here is 1, it was 7, and six had no gate.

I fixed it as orchestrator glue and recorded it as a deviation — no Phase 3 package owns `src/hooks/`, so there was no implementer to route it to. I did **not** take the deeper fix: `buildHostBundle()` is called twice in that file, so the bundle builds at least twice per run, and memoising it (the Phase 6 `vsce ls` treatment) would roughly halve its 19 s. But the second call site asserts the staged copy matches the on-disk artifact byte-for-byte, and the retry loop guards a truncate-then-write race against `extension.test.ts` building concurrently. That needs reasoning through properly, not a performance change smuggled into a gate. It's recorded as a follow-up.

**One correction to the runner's report:** it flagged `privacy.test.ts` as "within 8% of its own 10,000 ms bound," reading the file's 9,249 ms wall clock. The assertion at line 998 is on `timingsMs.historyMs` — the history *leg*, measured at 1,032 ms. That's ~10× headroom, not 8%. No action needed, and worth stating plainly because the two numbers look alike and one of them would have had me optimising something that isn't tight.

Confirming suite run and the DoD verification are both running now.

Diagnosed, and the cause is my own orchestration error.

**Uncontended, same commit:**

```
[perf]   .tailPoll     : median 6.8 ms   (vs 866.4 ms in the failing run)
[perf]   .incremental  : median 12.3 ms  (vs 872.9 ms)

```

**127× difference on identical code.** And `budgets.ts:199-209` says what `tailPoll` actually measures: *"Mostly the per-poll discovery sweep (readdir of the slug directory)"* — a filesystem `readdir`, the single most contention-sensitive thing in the suite.

The evidence chain:

| run | what else was running | tailPoll | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | test-runner alone | 12.6 ms | MET |
| 2 | test-runner **+ phase-verifier** | 866.4 ms | NOT MET |
| 3 | perf alone | 6.8 ms | MET |

Runs 2 and 3 are the same commit. **I dispatched the verifier concurrently with the suite** — and the verifier's job is read-only SQLite queries across 25 MB of new fixtures plus git history walks. I pointed a heavy I/O workload at the disk while a `readdir`-bound perf budget was measuring it. `projects.Sync.Service` sitting at 4,328 CPU-seconds over this projects-hosted repo, freshly given 25 MB of binary fixtures and a repacked `.git`, is the background contributor; my concurrent dispatch is the trigger.

**No production source changed in Phase 3** — `git diff --name-only release/0.5.0..HEAD -- src/ webview/` filtered of `.test.ts` returns nothing. Three test files, that's all.

**I'm not touching the budget.** Widening a perf limit to absorb I/O contention is the same move as widening the CC version window — it converts a real signal into a countdown, and this repo has shipped that defect twice. The budget correctly reported what it measured; the environment was wrong, and the environment was my fault.

I'm holding the confirming suite run until the verifier finishes, so the two don't contend again. Running them in parallel was the mistake and repeating it would just reproduce the failure.

Standing tally, pending that clean run: **1,574 passed + the 2 perf budgets verified green in isolation = 1,576, with 1 skip fully attributed** (`AGENT_DECK_PACKAGE_AUDIT`), typecheck and lint clean on both projects.

## DEVIATIONS — where the contract, the spec and `src/model/events.ts` do not line up

Each of these is a place the golden had to represent something the current type cannot express.
None was resolved by this package; all three are Phase 4's.

1. **`SessionState.engine` does not exist in `src/model/events.ts`.** OC7 specifies
   `engine?: 'cc' | 'opencode'`, additive and optional, absence reading as `'cc'`. The field is in
   both goldens because the spec says so; the interface has not been widened yet, so
   `src/release/opencode-golden.test.ts` validates against a local mirror of the shape rather than
   importing the interface. Phase 4 adds the field.

2. **`ParkCode` has no `taskWithoutChild`.** OC3 names it normatively ("the grafter parks the part
   with a stable code (`taskWithoutChild`, `PLAN.md` DoD 4.4)"); the union in `src/model/events.ts`
   carries the eight CC codes and not this one. The goldens use it. Phase 4 widens the union — and
   should decide at the same time whether `joinKeyContradiction` is a new code or should reuse the
   existing `parentAgentContradiction`.

3. **`ParkedGraft.agentId` is the wrong field for this case.** OpenCode parks a **part**, not an
   agent, and the case is defined by the child session id being absent. The goldens put the `prt_*`
   row id there because it is the only stable identity available. Either `ParkedGraft` gains an
   optional part id, or the field is documented as "the identity of the thing that did not graft",
   which is a wider claim than it makes today.

4. **`SpawnEdge.recordedDepth` says nothing for this engine.** It is documented as "`spawnDepth` as
   written in the sidecar, kept even when it disagrees" — the point being that a recorded value can
   contradict a walked one. OpenCode records **no** depth anywhere; depth is walked from `parent_id`
   (OC3). It therefore equals `depth` by construction in every edge in both goldens, and it can
   never disagree. It is not wrong, it is vacuous.

5. **`ToolNode` cannot carry `state.metadata.truncated`.** Contract §8.4 calls it "the flag to
   trust" for OpenCode's own truncation, and 14 anchor tool parts set it. `ToolNode` has no field
   for it, so the golden does not represent it — a payload OpenCode already truncated and one it did
   not are indistinguishable in these files.

6. **No non-`task` error tool part exists in the anchor.** All 27 error parts are `task` parts. The
   `resultPreview`-from-`state.error` rule is therefore only exercised on task calls in the anchor;
   the witness's single error part is a non-task tool and covers it there.

   with a stable code (`taskWithoutChild`, `PLAN.md` DoD 4.4)"); the union in `src/model/events.ts`
   carries the eight CC codes and not this one. The goldens use it. Phase 4 widens the union — and
   should decide at the same time whether `joinKeyContradiction` is a new code or should reuse the
   existing `parentAgentContradiction`.

3. **`ParkedGraft.agentId` is the wrong field for this case.** OpenCode parks a **part**, not an
   agent, and the case is defined by the child session id being absent. The goldens put the `prt_*`
   row id there because it is the only stable identity available. Either `ParkedGraft` gains an
   optional part id, or the field is documented as "the identity of the thing that did not graft",
   which is a wider claim than it makes today.

4. **`SpawnEdge.recordedDepth` says nothing for this engine.** It is documented as "`spawnDepth` as
   written in the sidecar, kept even when it disagrees" — the point being that a recorded value can
   contradict a walked one. OpenCode records **no** depth anywhere; depth is walked from `parent_id`
   (OC3). It therefore equals `depth` by construction in every edge in both goldens, and it can
   never disagree. It is not wrong, it is vacuous.

5. **`ToolNode` cannot carry `state.metadata.truncated`.** Contract §8.4 calls it "the flag to
   trust" for OpenCode's own truncation, and 14 anchor tool parts set it. `ToolNode` has no field
   for it, so the golden does not represent it — a payload OpenCode already truncated and one it did
   not are indistinguishable in these files.

   `resultPreview`-from-`state.error` rule is therefore only exercised on task calls in the anchor;
   the witness's single error part is a non-task tool and covers it there.

git diff --name-only release/0.5.0..HEAD -- src/ webview/ filtered of *.test.ts
returns nothing. The three test files that moved are two new ones and one
timeout argument.

FOUR USER DECISIONS THAT OVERRODE THE DoD's WORDING

1. G8 is filter-then-assert, not abort. The live database grew foreign project
   rows between planning and dispatch, making a literal "abort on any foreign
   project row" unsatisfiable. The capture selects this repo's project and
   asserts G8 twice — over the selection and again over the finished fixture —
   throwing on violation. Excluded: two sessions in two foreign projects.
2. Verbatim, no truncation. Verified against bytes rather than prose: the
   verifier compared 1,062 + 411 rows of message.data and part.data against the

   length(CAST(data AS BLOB)) so a UTF-8 round-trip failure a JS string compare

   pair is what proves that field optional. A single corpus could not.
4. Golden is the full tree for both corpora PLUS a hand-verified core of five

three calls, all under fixtures/ or an explicit --out; the live database is only
ever opened { readOnly: true }, and a write through that handle throws
ERR_SQLITE_ERROR errcode 8. The test strips comments before matching, because
its first version passed on the script's own prose.

G4 is non-vacuous. The corpora carry 427,928 and 227,011 characters of reasoning
text, and the goldens are searched for the first 64 bytes of every reasoning
part, raw and JSON-escaped: 0 hits. The suite additionally asserts the needle set
is non-empty, so the search cannot silently have nothing to find.

The golden generator is independent BY ASSERTION: its imports are node:buffer,
crypto, fs, path, url and sqlite, and nothing from src/. src/opencode/ does not
exist yet, and a golden sharing code with the engine it checks would prove
nothing.

# HANDOVER — v0.5.0 Phase 3 — CLOSED

**Branch `release/0.5.0`, merged at `fc7dbb8`.** Phase 3 (spec amendment + OpenCode fixture
harvest) is closed. **Next phase is 4** — the OpenCode engine core, `src/opencode/`.

**This document supersedes the previous handoff, which said Phase 3 was next.** `CLAUDE.md`'s
"Current state" block is updated in the same commit. A closed phase whose state documents still
open on an earlier one is this repo's most-repeated defect and PLAN.md records it against itself.

**Phase 3 needed no live OpenCode session.** The previous handoff said it would (§7). That was
measured wrong: the database already held every DoD 3.3 item. One fewer human dependency, and the
six human-only items in `CLAUDE.md` are unchanged by this phase.

---

## 1. Gates — measured on `1c10a17`, with nothing else dispatched

`git diff --stat 1c10a17 fc7dbb8` is **empty**: the merge commit's tree is byte-identical to the
gate commit's, so these results apply to `fc7dbb8` unchanged. Stated rather than assumed, because
a gate table written into the commit it describes is the defect this repo records most often.

| Gate | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Suite | `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` | **43 files passed, 1576 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**, exit 0 |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | **exit 0**, both tsc projects, no output |
| Lint | `npm run lint` | **exit 0**, no output |
| Smoke — spike audit | `CLAUDE_PROJECTS_ROOT=fixtures/cc-2.1.234/projects node spike/run.mjs --audit --project <abs> --all` | **RESOLVED 5, AMBIGUOUS 0, UNRESOLVED 0, spawnDepth mismatches 0, malformed 0, VERDICT DETERMINISTIC**, exit 0 |
| Privacy sweep | `node scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs --untracked` | **exit 0**, `unexpected=0 secrets=0 foreign=0`, 1,231 non-gating advisories |

**The suite moved 1445 → 1576, and the arithmetic closes exactly:** +53 from
`src/release/opencode-capture.test.ts` and +78 from `src/release/opencode-golden.test.ts`. No
existing test was deleted, renamed or weakened.

**The one skip is accounted for BY GATE, not against a number:** `src/release/vsix.test.ts`,
`runIf(AGENT_DECK_PACKAGE_AUDIT === '1')`. The other three environment gates ran **live** on this
box — both `skipIf(!WSL.usable)` in `src/model/pathmatrix.test.ts` (53 tests) and
`skipIf(LIVE_SETTINGS === null)` in `src/release/readme.test.ts` (27 tests). On a runner without
WSL the healthy count is ~7.

**The suite was NOT re-run after the merge.** The trees are identical and re-confirming green you
already have is a standing user direction against, not an omission.

---

## 2. What landed

14 commits, 16 files, +25,179 / −1,629.

| File | | |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-deck-spec.md` | +368 | the OpenCode amendment, OC1–OC10 |
| `scripts/capture-opencode.mjs` | 1,301 | the capture procedure |
| `scripts/opencode-golden.mjs` | 871 | the golden generator |
| `src/release/opencode-capture.test.ts` | 746 | 53 tests |
| `src/release/opencode-golden.test.ts` | 834 | 78 tests |
| `fixtures/opencode-1.18.22/` | | **THE ANCHOR** — 24 sessions, `opencode.db` 19,374,080 bytes, `README.md`, `GOLDEN.md`, `golden.json` |
| `fixtures/opencode-1.18.21/` | | the **witness** — 5 sessions, `opencode.db` 5,763,072 bytes, `README.md`, `golden.json` |
| `scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs` | +46 | three ALLOW rules |
| `fixtures/README.md` | +64 | corpus entries; the stale "private" claim corrected |
| `docs/evidence/privacy/report.json` | | regenerated |
| `src/hooks/egress.test.ts` | +12/−1 | a hook timeout — see §5 |

**No production source was touched.** `git diff --name-only 79b2879 fc7dbb8 -- src/ webview/`
filtered of `*.test.ts` returns nothing. Three test files moved: two new, one timeout argument.

**Disk cost of the verbatim decision:** 25,137,152 bytes of binary fixture pack to roughly 5.6 MB —
the witness deltifies against the anchor to 609 KB, since they share a schema and content. The
**whole repository pack is 9.27 MiB**, which is the entire clone cost, not an increment on a large
base.

---

## 3. Work-package map

Four packages, partitioned by file ownership. **No boundary violation by any implementer, and no
merge conflict** — every merge was clean.

| Package | Owned | DoD | Landed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P3-SPEC** | `agent-deck-spec.md` | 3.1 | `9a28c4d` |
| **P3-CAPTURE** | `scripts/capture-opencode.mjs`, `src/release/opencode-capture.test.ts`, both corpora except `golden.json` | 3.2, 3.3 | `baf0a00` |
| **P3-SWEEP** | `scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs`, `fixtures/README.md`, `docs/evidence/privacy/report.json` | 3.5 | `56e115d` |
| **P3-GOLDEN** | `scripts/opencode-golden.mjs`, both `golden.json`, `GOLDEN.md`, `src/release/opencode-golden.test.ts` | 3.4 | (merged after `56e115d`) |

Wave 1 was SPEC ∥ CAPTURE, merged **SPEC first** so DoD 3.1's "committed before 3.3" holds in
history. Wave 2 was GOLDEN ∥ SWEEP.

**P3-GOLDEN was interrupted mid-work** — its five files existed but were all untracked and its
branch had no commit. It was **resumed, not respawned**, and finished cleanly. Worth knowing that
the failure mode exists: an agent can stop with complete-looking output and nothing committed.

**Four orchestrator deviations, all documentation or test infrastructure, none production code:**

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `b3716ca` | A sweep ALLOW reason named the wrong needle and asserted a SQLite constraint that does not exist; `fixtures/README.md` still called this public repo private |
| `634d065` | `src/hooks/egress.test.ts` — the hook timeout, §5 |
| `1c10a17` | `GOLDEN.md` said "all three" over a list of six deviations, and items 5–6 are not Phase 4's work at all |
| `c6f25cf` | Regenerated the privacy report **after** the sweep change, in that order |

---

## 4. Four user decisions that overrode the DoD's wording

Recorded because a reader comparing PLAN.md to the repo will otherwise see a mismatch and
"fix" it.

1. **G8 is filter-then-assert, not abort.** DoD 3.2 says the capture "aborts on any `project` row
   whose `worktree` is not this repo". The live DB grew foreign project rows between planning and
   dispatch, making that literally unsatisfiable. The capture now selects this repo's project and
   asserts G8 **twice** — over the selection, and again over the finished fixture — throwing on
   violation. Excluded: 2 sessions across 2 foreign projects.
2. **Verbatim — nothing truncated.** DoD 3.2 permits truncating "other long payloads to shape".
   The user declined. Verified against bytes: the verifier compared **1,062 + 411 rows** of
   `message.data` and `part.data` against the **live** database, 0 mismatches.
3. **Two corpora, not one.** DoD 3.3 says one directory. The two known `compaction` shapes split
   across versions, so the pair is what proves `tail_start_id` optional.
4. **Golden is the full tree for both corpora PLUS a hand-verified core** of five worked cases in
   `GOLDEN.md`.

---

## 5. The gate failure that was diagnosed, not re-rolled

The first gate run failed `src/hooks/egress.test.ts`. Not an assertion — a `beforeAll` running a
synchronous esbuild subprocess carried **no timeout argument**, so it took vitest's 10 s default and
lost under the heavier suite. The fix was already in the same file: the sibling hook at line 600
closes `}, 120_000)`.

**Why it mattered more than a timeout usually does.** The summary read
`Tests 1570 passed | 7 skipped` with **no failed-test count at all** — a suite-level failure
contributes none. The timeout marked the whole describe as six skips, and **six G5 zero-egress
assertions over the shipped bundle ran zero times** while the tests line looked clean. What caught
it was requiring every skip to be attributed **by gate**: four gates exist, the healthy count here
is 1, it was 7.

The second run then failed **two `src/perf/perf.test.ts` budgets**, `tailPoll` at 866.4 ms against
150 ms. That was **my orchestration error**, not a regression: I had dispatched `phase-verifier`
concurrently, and it was running read-only SQLite queries across 25 MB of new fixtures.
`budgets.ts:199-209` records `tailPoll` as "mostly the per-poll discovery sweep (readdir of the
slug directory)" — filesystem-bound. Alone on the same commit it measured **6.8 ms**; on the final
clean suite run **7.3 ms**.

**The budget was not widened.** It reported what it measured. Widening a limit to absorb contention
is how a real signal becomes a countdown — the version-window lesson, applied to timing.

---

## 6. Open items and risks

**Owed by Phase 4, from the verifier and `GOLDEN.md`:**

1. **Four type/spec disagreements.** `SessionState.engine` is spec'd by OC7 but absent from
   `src/model/events.ts` (the golden test validates against a local mirror); `ParkCode` has no
   `taskWithoutChild` although OC3 names it normatively; `ParkedGraft.agentId` is the wrong field
   for a **part**-level park (the goldens put the `prt_*` id there because no agent id exists —
   which *is* the case); `SpawnEdge.recordedDepth` equals `depth` by construction and can never
   disagree, because OpenCode records no depth.
2. **Ten unexercised branches**, tabulated in `GOLDEN.md`. Including `liveness: "live"`, which a
   static fixture cannot produce **by construction**, and `ToolNode.status: "running"`, of which
   the corpora contain none. **Phase 4 will reproduce both goldens without proving any of the ten**
   — do not read a reproduction as full coverage.
3. **The `synthetic-` fixture for an unopenable database is still owed** (contract §7, carried from
   Phase 2). OpenCode *dying* with a hot WAL was never reproduced; the ordinary hot-WAL case is
   measured as a non-event.
4. **The version window is deliberately not applied** in the goldens — OC5 makes it Phase 4's. Both
   goldens carry `schemaOk: true`. If Phase 4's window excludes `1.18.21`, that golden becomes a
   golden of `unsupported` sessions and must be regenerated.

**Owed by Phase 5:**

5. **`SessionState.projectSlug` has no OpenCode answer.** The field is named for CC's slug directory
   and OpenCode has no slug. The goldens carry `""` as an explicit placeholder, marked as such in
   three places. PLAN.md DoD 5.1/5.2 do not decide it either. **This is a real gap in the plan.**

**Standing risks the verifier raised:**

6. **FOREIGN cannot fire inside the two OpenCode corpora.** The ALLOW rules are whole-directory
   prefixes, so foreign content reaching those `.db` files would be advisory, never gating.
   `assertG8()` in the capture script is the only real defence — **one layer, not two**, and it
   holds only while that script remains the sole way those files are produced.
7. **The privacy advisory list has stopped being a review surface**: 19 → **1,231**, driven by
   scanning 25 MB of tracked binary. The gate is unaffected and all three counters are zero, but a
   genuinely novel advisory shape is now invisible by volume.
8. **The verbatim cross-check has a shelf life.** The strongest 3.2 evidence is a byte compare
   against the live database, which still holds the captured sessions. Once OpenCode ages them out,
   "verbatim" is checkable only through the capture script's own internal verification —
   self-consistent, but no longer independently falsifiable.
9. **`docs/evidence/privacy/report.json` is now 1.1 MB** and grows on every regeneration. Truncation
   was deliberately not added: no rule truncates today and inventing one would change what the
   report means for every other rule. A repo-weight question for a later phase.
10. **`src/release/workflow.test.ts` carries a stale "the repository is private" claim** in a file
    header comment. Not fixed — it is a comment, not an assertion, and this phase does not otherwise
    touch that file.

---

## 7. First actions for Phase 4

**Entry point:** `PLAN.md` → *Phase 4 — OpenCode engine core*. Branch `phase-4-oc-engine` off
`release/0.5.0`. Packages, one worktree each: `P4-DB` (`db.ts`, `fingerprint.ts`) · `P4-PARSE`
(`parse.ts`, `redact` reuse) · `P4-GRAFT` (`graft.ts`) · `P4-LIVE` (`liveness.ts`). The orchestrator
owns `src/opencode/index.ts` only.

**Read first, in this order:**

1. `agent-deck-spec.md` → **`## Amendment 2026-08-27 — Second observation source: OpenCode`**
   (line 305). **This is now the spec**, and it supersedes chat and the contract doc where they
   disagree. Note it sits **before** the version-posture amendment, not last — see §8.
2. `fixtures/opencode-1.18.22/GOLDEN.md` — the mapping decisions, the hand-verified five, the
   DEVIATIONS list, and the ten unexercised branches.
3. `docs/opencode-contract.md` **including its `Amendment 2026-08-26` section (§A–§H)**.
4. This document's §6.

**Phase 4 must reproduce both `golden.json` files through the production path.**
`scripts/opencode-golden.mjs` is the reference, and it is independent by assertion — it imports only
`node:` builtins. **Do not make the engine import it, or the goldens stop proving anything.**

**Phase 7 is also unblocked** (`docs/ui/design.md` is `FROZEN 26082026` — match on `FROZEN`, not on
a date format), but Phase 4 comes first in PLAN order.

---

## 8. State

| | |
|---|---|
| `release/0.5.0` | `fc7dbb8`, clean tree, **32 commits ahead of `origin/release/0.5.0` — NOT PUSHED** |
| `main` | `624b10c`, untouched. `v0.1.2` live on the Marketplace |
| Tags | `v0.1.0`, `v0.1.1`, `v0.1.2` |
| Worktrees | **one** — the repo itself. All four Phase 3 worker worktrees removed |
| Branches retained | `phase-3-oc-spec-harvest` and the four `worktree-agent-*`, all merged and recoverable |
| Repo pack | 9.27 MiB |

**Pushing is the one thing this session did not do**, exactly as the previous handoff also ended.
`origin` is public and the repo's rule is that pushes happen when asked. 32 commits are waiting.

**The spec amendment is placed BEFORE the version-posture amendment, not appended last.**
`src/release/readme.test.ts:571-574` slices the version-posture section to EOF and asserts it holds
no later `## ` heading, so appending fails. Placing before also keeps the CC version guards from
scanning OpenCode's `1.18.x` strings and reading them as CC anchor claims. Both the date
(`2026-08-27`, its authoring date, where DoD 3.1 says the planning date) and the placement are
recorded inside the section itself.

---

## 9. How this document was validated

`test-runner` produced §1's suite counts; the smoke, sweep, typecheck and lint lines were run
directly in this session by the command shown beside each. `phase-verifier` audited DoD 3.1–3.5
against repository state and returned **PASS**, then audited this document's claims. Every number
here comes from a command in this session, not from memory.

**One correction made during the gate, recorded because it changed a decision:** `test-runner`
reported `privacy.test.ts` as "within ~8% of its own 10,000 ms bound", reading the file's 9,249 ms
wall clock. The assertion at `privacy.test.ts:998` is on `timingsMs.historyMs` — the history **leg**,
measured at 1,032 ms. That is ~10× headroom, not 8%, and the difference is the difference between
optimising something and leaving it alone.

- **SQLite `LIKE` is CASE-INSENSITIVE for ASCII, and it will hand you a confident wrong answer.**
  Phase 3 measured 69 hits for a foreign project name and alarming counts for `ACCESS_TOKEN`,

  with **`GLOB`**: **zero**, every one. `LIKE '%ERW%'` was matching `ov`+`erw`+`rite`, and
  `ACCESS_TOKEN` was matching this repo's own prose about `access_token` columns. **Any needle,
  secret or G8 check over a SQLite corpus must use `GLOB` or `instr()`** — the same family as the
  `grep -a` trap, reached through a different tool.

- **A `beforeAll` that shells out has vitest's 10 s DEFAULT hookTimeout, and when it loses the race
  the failure reports as SKIPS with a clean-looking tests line.** `src/hooks/egress.test.ts:242`
  ran esbuild in a hook with no timeout argument; Phase 3's added suite weight pushed it over, and
  the summary read `1570 passed | 7 skipped` with **no failed-test count at all**, because a
  suite-level failure contributes none. Six G5 zero-egress assertions ran zero times. The sibling
  hook in the same file already carried `}, 120_000)`. **This is the "fails to COLLECT, reports as
  skipped, reads green" class arriving by a new route** — a hook timeout rather than an import
  error — and the only thing that catches it is accounting for every skip **by GATE**.

- **`src/perf/perf.test.ts`'s `tailPoll` budget is filesystem-bound and will fail if you run
  anything heavy beside the suite.** `budgets.ts:199-209` records it as "mostly the per-poll
  discovery sweep (readdir of the slug directory)". Measured on one commit: **866.4 ms** with a
  `phase-verifier` concurrently running read-only SQLite queries over 25 MB of fixtures, against a
  150 ms limit and a 12.0 ms set point — and **6.8-7.3 ms** with the suite run alone. **Never
  dispatch `test-runner` and `phase-verifier` concurrently**, and never widen the budget to absorb
  it: the limit reported exactly what it measured, and widening a limit to survive contention is
  the version-window mistake in timing form.

- **A whole-directory ALLOW prefix in the privacy sweep means FOREIGN can never fire inside it.**
  The two `capture-opencode-*` rules are directory prefixes, so foreign content reaching those
  `.db` files would be raised as an advisory and never gate. The only real defence is
  `assertG8()` inside `scripts/capture-opencode.mjs` — **one layer, not two**, and it holds only
  while that script stays the sole way those fixtures are produced. Related: the advisory list went
  19 → **1,231** on 25 MB of tracked binary, so it has stopped being a review surface; a novel
  advisory shape is now invisible by volume.

- **A committed SQLite fixture is far cheaper in git than its file size suggests.** 25,137,152
  bytes across two corpora pack to roughly **5.6 MB**, and the second deltifies against the first
  down to 609 KB because they share a schema and overlapping rows. The whole repo pack is 9.27 MiB.

# Phase 3 is closed

Merged at `fc7dbb8`, handoff committed at `f6c1564`, tree clean.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Suite | **43 files, 1576 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**, exit 0 |
| Typecheck | exit 0, both tsc projects |
| Lint | exit 0 |
| Smoke — spike audit | RESOLVED 5, AMBIGUOUS 0, UNRESOLVED 0, **DETERMINISTIC**, exit 0 |
| Privacy sweep `--untracked` | exit 0, `unexpected=0 secrets=0 foreign=0` |
| Verifier, DoD 3.1–3.5 | **PASS** |

The suite moved 1445 → 1576 and the arithmetic closes exactly: +53 and +78 from the two new files, counted with `vitest list`. Four packages, **no boundary violation and no merge conflict** — ownership re-verified per merge against the merge-base.

**The verifier failed my first draft, 31 of 38 items.** All seven corrections are in the commit, and the worst one was mine: the new CLAUDE.md constraint claimed case-sensitive `GLOB` returns "zero, every one." Measured, that's true for `ACCESS_TOKEN` (10→0) and `github_pat` (9→0) but **false for `api_key` (21→14) and `password` (17→17)**. The survivors are benign — OpenCode's own docs and this repo's sessions quoting the sweep's needle list, and `secrets=0` holds because the sweep keys on high-entropy *assignment shape*, not the bare word. But as written it would have taught the next agent that zero is expected, and they'd have escalated on 17 hits of the word "password." I'd written a false constraint into the file whose entire purpose is preventing re-learned mistakes. The others were the same family: two line-deltas read from git's *changed-lines* column, three stale `file:line` pointers (one written from inside the commit that moved it), and a "direct quote" missing two words.

One I want to name because it's ironic: the skip table quoted whole-*file* test counts (53, 27) as *gate* sizes. That's exactly the arithmetic the "account for every skip by gate" rule exists to prevent — in the document that preaches it.

**Six new constraints** in CLAUDE.md, the load-bearing ones being: `LIKE` is case-insensitive and `GLOB` is not a synonym for zero; a `beforeAll` that shells out inherits vitest's 10 s default and **fails as skips with no failed-test count**; and `tailPoll` is readdir-bound, so never dispatch `test-runner` and `phase-verifier` together — my own error, which cost a gate run.

**Two things need you:**

**32 commits are unpushed.** `origin` is public and this repo's rule is that pushes happen when asked. Say the word.

**`SessionState.projectSlug` has no OpenCode answer** — the field is named for CC's slug directory and OpenCode has no slug. The goldens carry `""` as an explicit placeholder, and PLAN.md's DoD 5.1/5.2 don't decide it either. That's a genuine gap in the plan, not just in the code.

Phase 4 also inherits **ten branches no fixture exercises** — including `liveness: "live"`, which a static fixture cannot produce *by construction*. It will reproduce both goldens without proving any of them, and that shouldn't be read as full coverage.

And still open from earlier: **the live addon dropping actions is unresolved**, with the diagnostics recorded. The phase is done, so that debugging window is open whenever you want it — I still don't know whether the addon is Agent Deck itself, which decides everything about where to look.
